title: The chief removes the folders that agents leave, and saves its own pages

long.title: The clean-up change is merged; the full description is on its page
long.main: the chief can now remove the leftover folders that agents leave, and save its own pages. Task worktrees stay safe. It works after you update sage.

blocks.label: Where this is
blocks.text: sage-stack › Release 1.0 › single task from your request of 7 Nov for fewer restrictions › merged on 10 Nov

body.text: In sage mode the chief changes no files of the project. An earlier change also refused the chief's shell writes outside the temp folder. So the chief could not remove the empty folders that its agents left in ~/sage-worktrees, and it could not save its own pages.
You decided on 7 Nov that the chief may do both.

rows: Clean-up of leftover folders
The chief removes leftover folders in ~/sage-worktrees itself. A folder that holds a git work tree stays: only git worktree remove works there, and git refuses a worktree with changes.
Tests in both apps. The first review found that the chief could remove a live task folder; the repair added the git rule and a test.
1.4 M tokens and about 2.5 h of agent time for the whole pull request (measured)
Yes: update sage
The chief's own pages and scratch files
The chief writes its pages into the task's pages folder, and its scratch files into the temp folder.
Tests in both apps; one clean cycle: code review clean, QA pass, checks pass.

head: Command of the chief
Decision
Reason
rows: rmdir or rm -rf of a leftover folder in ~/sage-worktrees that holds no git work tree
Runs
The chief cleans up what its runs left.
git worktree remove of a task worktree
Runs
git refuses a worktree with changes, so no work is lost.
rm -rf of a git work tree, a write into one, or git worktree remove --force
Refused
A work tree holds repository files and maybe work that is not committed.
A write of a page into the task's pages folder (cat, tee, cp, touch)
Runs
The chief saves its own research pages and notes.
rm, mv and cp inside the temp folder
Runs
Scratch work.
Any write with a target in the project
Refused
Repository files stay with an implementer.
A write into ~/.claude, another home folder, or the logbook
Refused
Only the scratch places count; the logbook rule stays.
A path with a variable or a pattern (rm $TMPDIR/x, rm /tmp/x/*)
Refused
The hook cannot name every target, so it refuses. Write the literal path.

blocks.text: seven small findings stay on the polish list. For example: git's forced remove still runs when its option name is shortened, and mkdir runs in every folder.
